problem: LINT-3's N5 heuristic fires HIGH on Recent-developments entries whose SUBJECT case is a circuit case when the 45-char window after the case name contains a descriptive bare 'SCOTUS' token ('-> superseded by SCOTUS'). Two live HIGHs: 'Standing to Challenge a Search.md':80 and 'The Exclusionary Rule.md':129 - both entries' subject is United States v. Chatrie (4th Cir. en banc, 136 F.4th 100), correctly placed as a superseded circuit development; the SCOTUS decision (Chatrie v. United States, 609 U.S. ___) is homed in Key cases elsewhere. The lint's own docstring promises passing references 'do NOT trigger'. A permanently-red HIGH teaches operators to ignore the roster (S1 A8's alarm-fatigue failure mode) and blocks a fail-closed CI gate on correct content.
proposed_fix: Suppress the SCOTUS-tag branch (not the reporter-cite branch) when a circuit-court reference (e.g. '4th Cir.', 'D.C. Cir.' - parenthesized or not; line 129 uses a backtick label, not parens) precedes the SCOTUS token inside the window: the entry's own court is named between the case name and the token, so the token is subsequent-history description, not the subject court. Ship a pass/fail fixture (scripts/lint/fixtures/lint-3-n5.md) proving both live FP shapes are suppressed AND true positives (U.S. reporter cite; '(SCOTUS)' tag with no preceding circuit ref) still fire.
